topics.title: Our Weather - Meaning of Weather Symbols | Weather Records and Charts Primary 4 (Basic 4) and Primary 6 (Basic 6) - Basic Science and Technology ASEI PDSI METHOD
topics.content:
BASIC SCIENCE (BST)
BASIC SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
SMASE - ASEI PDSI METHOD
FIRST TERM
WEEK 6/PRIMARY 4
WEEK 4/PRIMARY 6
THEME - LEARNING ABOUT OUR ENVIRONMENT
PREVIOUS LESSON - Meaning of Weather and Factors Affecting the Weather (Primary 4) ASEI PDSI METHOD
TOPIC - OUR WEATHER
LEARNING AREA
Lesson One - Meaning and Symbols of Weather
Lesson Two - Weather Records and Chart
Lesson Three - Revision and Test
TIME - 40 Minutes each.
LEARNING OUTCOME
By the end of the lesson, pupils should be able to:
1. identify and write simple weather symbols;
2. observe weather changes over a period of about three weeks;
3. use the weather symbols to keep records of weather changes;
4. prepare a weather chart.
RATIONALE
Weather is the state of the atmosphere at a particular time. The following are weather symbols sunny, cloudy, cloudy with sunshine, sunny with rainfall, cloudy with thunder, etc. representing the the sun, the rainfall, the cloud, the wind, etc.
Weather symbols are used internationally to communicate the weather forecast to people. The value of using a symbol is that it contains no words and can therefore be easy to understand.
The concept of weather, symbols and charts will enable the pupils to understand and records weather of the day using appropriate symbols.
LEARNING MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of:
Weather symbols
Weather chart
Cardboard
Writing materials
PREVIOUS KNOWLEDGE
The pupils can tell when it cloudy and about to rain. They are aware of different things that comes along with the rain - storm  thunder, wind, dust, etc. After rainy season comes the dry season, sunny days.

WEEK 5/PRIMARY 6 - EARTH AND SKY MOVEMENT
PREVIOUS LESSON - Changes in Non Living Things Primary 4 (Basic 4) - Basic Science and Technology
TOPIC - OUR WEATHER
LEARNING AREA
Lesson One - Meaning and Factors Affecting the Weather
Lesson Two - Weather Instruments
Lesson Three - Revision and Test
TIME - 40 Minutes each.
LEARNING OUTCOME
By the end of the lesson, pupils should be able to:
1. state the meaning of weather.
2. identify the factors affecting the weather.
3. name the standard weather instruments.
RATIONALE
Weather is the state of the atmosphere at a particular time.
Weather are important for planning our day to activities especially in farming and production of goods and services and instruments used for these planning is called weather instruments.
The sun, cloud, wind, temperature and moisture (rain) are factors that affect our day to day favourable weather.
The concept of weather will enable people to understand and appreciate the importance of weather in planning.
LEARNING MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of:
A chart showing the weather conditions.
A chart showing the weather instruments.
PREVIOUS KNOWLEDGE
The pupils can tell when it cloudy and about to rain.
They are aware of different things that comes along with the rain - storm  thunder, wind, dust, etc.

topics.title: Basic Science and Technology - 50 Multiple Choice Questions (MCQs) with Answer Key for Primary 6
topics.content:
BASIC SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY - 50 MULTIPLE CHOICE QUESTIONS (MCQs) WITH ANSWER KEY FOR PRIMARY 6
INSTRUCTION - Choose the correct answer from the options A - D.
1. Air is a mixture of _____. A. liquids only B. solids C. water D. gases
2. The gas needed for breathing is _____. A. nitrogen B. oxygen C. carbon dioxide D. hydrogen
3. Moving air is called _____. A. breeze B. storm C. wind D. cloud
4. Which of these shows that air occupies space? A. Air has colour B. Inflated balloon C. Air has taste D. Air has sound
5. Climate change means _____. A. daily weather changes B. rainfall only C. hot afternoons D. long-term change in weather conditions
6. One cause of climate change is _____. A. tree planting B. deforestation C. recycling D. rainfall
7. Burning fossil fuels releases _____. A. oxygen B. nitrogen C. carbon dioxide D. hydrogen
8. One effect of climate change is _____. A. stable seasons B. flooding C. fresh air D. planting trees
9. The Earth rotates on its _____. A. orbit B. surface C. moon D. axis
10. One complete rotation of the Earth causes _____. A. a year B. a month C. day and night D. seasons
11. The movement of the Earth around the sun is called _____. A. Revolution B. rotation C. vibration D. motion
12. One complete revolution of the Earth takes _____. A. 24 hours B. 7 days C. 30 days D. 365 days
13. The solar system has _____ at the center. A. the moon B. Earth C. the sun D. Mars
14. Which of these is NOT a planet? A. Earth B. Moon C. Venus D. Mars
15. The planet closest to the sun is _____. A. Earth B. Venus C. Mercury D. Mars
16. The largest planet in the solar system is _____. A. Earth B. Jupiter C. Saturn D. Uranus
17. Colours seen when sunlight passes through rain are called _____. A. shadow B. spectrum C. reflection D. mirror
18. The three primary colours are _____. A. red, blue, yellow B. green, orange, purple C. black, white, grey D. pink, brown, gold
19. Mixing red and blue gives _____. A. green B. yellow C. purple D. orange
20. White colour reflects _____. A. no light B. some light C. red light D. all light
21. The smallest particle of an element is called _____. A. molecule B. cell C. Compound D. atom
22. An element is a substance that _____. A. contains many compounds B. cannot be broken into simpler substances C. is always liquid D. has colour
23. Oxygen is an example of _____. A. element B. compound C. mixture D. solution
24. Elements are arranged in the _____. A. timetable B. register C. periodic table D. notebook
25. Woodwork is the art of working with _____. A. metal B. plastic C. wood D. glass
26. A saw is used for _____. A. painting B. cutting wood C. measuring D. drilling
27. A hammer is used for _____. A. pulling nails B. cutting wood C. fixing nails D. sanding wood
28. A tape rule is used for _____. A. measuring B. cutting C. nailing D. shaping
29. Maintenance means _____. A. destroying tools B. repairing and caring for tools C. hiding tools D. selling tools
30. One reason for maintaining tools is to _____. A. spoil them B. lose them C. rust them D. make them last longer
31. Oiling metal tools helps to prevent _____. A. cutting B. rusting C. breaking D. bending
32. Tools should be stored in a _____. A. classroom B. cupboard or toolbox C. playground D. dustbin
33. Safety means _____. A. freedom from danger B. playing carelessly C. running everywhere D. breaking rules
34. Wearing goggles in the workshop helps to protect the _____. A. hands B. feet C. eyes D. ears
35. One safety rule in the workshop is to _____. A. run around B. misuse tools C. follow instructions D. joke with tools
36. Sharp tools should be handled _____. A. carelessly B. playfully C. carefully D. wrongly
37. Carbon dioxide is useful to plants for _____. A. breathing B. photosynthesis C. sleeping D. eating
38. Flooding can be reduced by _____. A. cutting trees B. planting trees C. burning bushes D. blocking drainage
39. The Earth gets light from the _____. A. moon B. stars C. sun D. clouds
40. The moon is a _____. A. planet B. star C. satellite D. comet
41. Mixing yellow and blue gives _____. A. orange B. green C. purple D. brown
42. Hydrogen is an example of _____. A. element B. mixture C. Compound D. solution
43. A chisel is mainly used in woodwork for _____. A. measuring B. cutting and shaping wood C. painting D. joining papers
44. Cleaning tools after use is an example of _____. A. misuse B. maintenance C. waste D. danger
45. Wearing gloves helps to protect the _____. A. hands B. eyes C. head D. legs
46. One effect of air pollution is _____. A. fresh air B. good health C. breathing problems D. clean sky
47. The layer of air around the Earth is called _____. A. hydrosphere B. atmosphere C. lithosphere D. biosphere
48. The sun is a _____. A. planet B. satellite C. asteroid D. star
49. A screwdriver is used to _____. A. cut wood B. tighten or loosen screws C. measure wood D. paint surfaces
50. Obeying safety rules helps to prevent _____. A. learning B. success C. fun D. accidents
ANSWER KEY
1. B 2. D 3. C 4. B 5. D 6. B 7. C 8. B 9. D 10. C
11. A 12. D 13. C 14. B 15. C 16. B 17. B 18. A 19. C 20. C
21. D 22. B 23. A 24. C 25. C 26. B 27. C 28. A 29. B 30. D
31. B 32. B 33. A 34. C 35. C 36. C 37. B 38. B 39. C 40. C
41. B 42. A 43. B 44. B 45. A 46. C 47. B 48. D 49. B 50. D
